subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, jitter, or prime-cadence controls for cron `every` schedules, or keep `every` as a fixed anchored interval while relying on heartbeat phase and cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior?
rationale: The remaining request changes public scheduling semantics, persisted cron shape, CLI flags, docs, and upgrade expectations, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product surface.

options.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
options.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, persistence, docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve `every` as an anchored interval and close or mark the cron portion not planned while relying on existing heartbeat phase and cron-expression stagger.

options.title: Accept broader prime mode
options.body: Add prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls across heartbeat and cron, with migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design narrow cron every phase/stagger contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit `every` scheduling contract with schema, CLI, persistence, docs, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the cron-expression stagger surface and has the strongest history on the remaining cron scheduling boundary.
